EPISODE 6

SCENE FOUR 

Esther is in the park with Mark.

MARK: I nailed it … hit out of the ballpark. And all I did was talk like you talk.  

ESTHER: Do I get royalties?

MARK: You are my muse.

ESTHER: Then how come you never listen to me? 

MARK: Of course I listen to you. You’re my funny-bone muse.

ESTHER: I don’t want to be a funny-bone muse. 

MARK: Well you are sweetheart. And all I had to do was pretend I was you … “You know what I hate about being a therapist - People coming to me with their problems.” You were a hit baby. 

Mark continues with his act. 

“So yesterday my day was shit - I even had to tell this client to try to be more sensitive … I was feeling a bit fragile and wasn’t sure I could cope with all his problems. But he just went on and on, talking about himself like I should be interested for fuck’s sake. What I really wanted to say was - Get it together man. Come back when you’ve sorted out your issues.”

ESTHER: This is not funny Mark. 

MARK (continuing his act): “Then the other afternoon some dumb ass woman sitting across from me suggested I might a narcissist … ‘of  course I’m a narcissist,’ I told her, ‘how else could I respond to your stupid questions without having to listen to you?’”

ESTHER: Stop it. 

MARK: “Besides, I need to spend my time thinking about me. My issues. Am I lovable? Am I as stupid as you? Why do I wear my heart on my sleeve? Is it too late to be a singer? Why do I throttle my passion? Why am I a coward … a coward … a coward? And how do I turn off the repeat button inside my head?” 

What I really wanted to say was “Listen little lady, if it wasn’t for me your words wouldn’t exist.”

You know something Esther. Being you is a dream. 

ESTHER: Stop.

MARK: What?

ESTHER. I mean Stop.

MARK: What’s wrong? 

ESTHER: Buster died …

MARK: Oh honey … I’m so sorry. 

They stop walking.

ESTHER: Breaks my heart really. 

MARK: I’m sure… I’m sure it does. 

ESTHER: Only knew him for a few hours and it just breaks my heart.

MARK: Can I do anything?

ESTHER: No, I think I have a girlfriend. 

MARK: That’s great. A girlfriend? 

ESTHER: Maybe.

MARK: What about me? 

ESTHER: Don’t be a narcissist.

MARK: Do you think I’m a narcissist?

ESTHER: I think you’re … I love you.

MARK: I love you too.

ESTHER: I have to go get dressed for the memorial service.

MARK: For the bow-wow.

ESTHER: Yes Mark, for the bow-wow.

MARK: Can I come? I can do some stand-up, some doggie stand-up.

ESTHER: No.

MARK: Okay - see you there. Where is it?

ESTHER: I said no.
…………………………………………………………………………
